Best,

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finhealth.com>

Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SOC 2 / Pen test report & vuln management next steps

Thanks Stephanie -- that sounds good. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- For SOC 2 we generally need either a SOC 2 Type II report or the AICPA bridge letter + control description. If you have a SOC 2 report we can sign an NDA and accept a redacted copy.
- For pen test: we typically ask for the last external pen test and a description of your remediation SLAs (critical/high/medium/low) plus how you handle disclosure to customers.
- Questionnaire: we'll start with the XLS and drop in any follow-ups.

Could you also confirm whether Redwood runs authenticated internal scans and external vulnerability scans, and the cadence (e.g., weekly internal, monthly external) and who owns triage?

Appreciate it -- Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Security Programs | FinHealth

From: David Kim <david.k@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finhealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SOC 2 / Pen test report & vuln management next steps

Hi Alex --

Following up with the details you requested. High level answers first, then attachments we can provide: 

1) SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II covering our production inference and control plane in Dec 2026. We can share a redacted SOC 2 report under an NDA. Evidence and control descriptions are available in the shared drive link Marissa will provide.

2) Pen test: Our most recent external pen test was conducted by RedShield in Aug 2026. We have a redacted executive summary attached (pen_test_report_2026_redacted.pdf). Full report is provided to customers under a standard NDA and Data Processing Agreement.

3) Vulnerability management (process & SLAs):
   - Scanning cadence: authenticated internal scans (weekly), external unauthenticated scans (monthly), on-demand scans for major releases or customer-reported issues.
   - Triage: Security Engineering owns initial triage (same-day acknowledgment). Engineering teams own remediation work with the following target SLAs based on severity (CVE scoring + business impact):
       * Critical: acknowledge within 24 hours, remediate or mitigation plan within 14 calendar days.
       * High: acknowledge within 48 hours, remediate within 30 calendar days.
       * Medium: acknowledge within 7 days, remediation within 90 calendar days.
       * Low: acknowledge within 14 days, remediation as per scheduled maintenance (6 months).
   - Disclosure: For customer-impacting findings, we notify affected customers within 72 hours of verification. For public disclosures we follow coordinated disclosure timelines with researchers and offer credits/bug-bounty coordination where applicable.
   - Escrow & remediation tracking: all findings are tracked in JIRA (SUP-XXXX style) and linked to customer tickets as needed.

Attachments included in this thread: redacted pen test summary, vendor questionnaire template. We'll also share the SOC 2 redacted PDF once the NDA is in place.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 20-minute call tomorrow for David or our Head of Security to walk through the SLAs and evidence.

Thanks,
David Kim
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pen_test_report_2026_redacted.pdf]

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finhealth.com>

Appreciate the quick breakdown David -- that covers most of our immediate questions. A couple follow-ups: 

- Please send the SOC 2 redacted report; we'll sign your NDA.
- For the remediation SLAs, FinHealth requires a max 30-calendar-day remediation window for high and critical findings that affect cardholder or PHI flows. Is Redwood able to commit to that for customers where PHI is in-scope?
- We'll populate the questionnaire and drop any clarifying questions into the sheet.

Marissa -- can you send over the DocuSign NDA and the shared drive folder link with evidence? Once the NDA is signed we'll review the SOC 2 and the full pen test.

Thanks -- Alex
